kaigo-depth-team-handoff.heading: Connect specific information and questions with professionals
paragraphs: Multidisciplinary coordination is more than remembering job titles. Start with the life the person wants, difficult situations and actual observations, then specify the consultation question. “Please ask a professional” alone may not convey enough information.

Physical therapists mainly address basic movement, occupational therapists daily-life activities, and speech-language therapists language, communication and swallowing. One difficulty may involve several areas. Rather than assigning everything from a title, confirm responsibilities and consultation contacts.

Care workers convey daily events in meals or activities, the person’s words and changes from usual. Separate successful and difficult parts and the conditions of difficulty to help recipients understand. Unconfirmed causes or diagnoses remain unconfirmed.

Sending a report, receipt, confirming advice and changing a support plan are separate states. Ask about unclear explanations and confirm who will provide which help and what may be changed before acting.

Keep wishes central and share the necessary scope with appropriate recipients. This lesson organizes roles and consultation; it does not instruct care workers to diagnose, independently design rehabilitation exercises or change food texture or drinks merely because a report was sent.

[Learning example] Kai-san wants club participation but struggles with arranging items by hand and speaking before a group. Staff sent only “PT, please handle everything.” Separate participation wishes, observed difficulties and desired advice, then clarify responsibility and consultation contacts. The speech difficulty’s cause is not diagnosed.

kaigo-depth-observation-evidence.heading: Record personal words, observations and measurements separately
paragraphs: Let readers identify information sources. Feelings and wishes, observed actions and measured values complement each other. Do not turn reported tiredness into a temperature or write a diagnosis from appearance alone.

When noticing a change, record known time and circumstances and what was observed during that period. Observation time differs from whether onset occurred earlier. Do not add unobserved periods or areas as confirmed.

If no value exists yet, report it as unmeasured. Staff feeling hot, measuring room temperature and measuring personal temperature are different. One impression or action must not become an established cause.

Near-miss or hazard records should lead to reporting and follow-up. No injury does not eliminate risk. Before causes are checked, avoid blame and review environment, equipment and methods with the team.

Correct unsupported conclusions using facility procedures and keep the correction identifiable. This teaches observation and measurement, not diagnostic or treatment thresholds. In urgent conditions, do not delay help or contact to polish text.

[Learning example] At 14:00 Lien-san said, “I am tired today,” and stopped towel folding twice. Nothing was measured, but the record says “fever due to room heat.” Preserve time, words and actions, correct unconfirmed fever and cause, and report the change to the person responsible.

kaigo-completeness-hand-choice.heading: Check hand-hygiene methods and completion
paragraphs: Before hand hygiene, check visible dirt, previous contacts and the next task. Water-and-soap washing differs from rubbing an alcohol product. Do not choose only for proximity or speed.

With visible dirt, wash using running water and soap. Reach required surfaces on both hands, including backs, webs, thumbs, fingertips and nail areas, not only palms. Check facility rules for rings and watches. Counting repetitions alone does not establish washing.

After soap washing, check rinsing and suitable drying too. For hand rub, use manufacturer quantity and method, distribute fully and rub until dry. Do not finish by wiping it off with paper before drying.
Touching a dirty towel or surface afterward can contaminate clean hands again. Check new contacts before the next task and perform hygiene at required times. Gloves do not replace hand hygiene.

This section teaches method differences, surfaces, completion and transition to the next task. Quantity, time and product- or pathogen-specific selection follow facility precautions, product instructions and practical training. Do not invent your own procedure from this text.

[Learning example] Hands are visibly dirty after collecting soiled towels. Colleagues propose hurried hand rubbing or gloves alone. Choose water and soap based on visible dirt, checking coverage, rinsing, drying and possible recontamination before the next task.

kaigo-completeness-worker-capacity.heading: Check personal condition and working requirements first
paragraphs: Reducing back strain requires checks of abilities, workspace, equipment, staffing and roles as well as posture. A wide stance does not establish safe solo movement of a person. Before accepting work, check whether the method suits both person and worker.

Report back pain, fatigue or difficulty working safely to the person responsible. Hiding pain and continuing by force can increase risk for both. Current worker health is information for reviewing support conditions.
Select lifts or sliding sheets for the person and task, inspect before use and use trained methods. Equipment in storage does not establish model knowledge or shared-work roles.
Report lack of training with unfamiliar equipment too. Confirm operator, plan and helpers. For full-assistance transfers, consider lifts and other methods avoiding reliance on manual lifting.

This teaches pre-task consultation and conditions, not lifting, pulling, transfer or bodily pivot techniques. Individual assessment, equipment handling and practical training are needed; do not try unclear methods alone.

[Learning example] A worker has back pain today and no training on the stored sliding-sheet model. Asked to reposition someone, they must not assume posture and equipment presence establish readiness. Report and check health, training, the person’s plan and helpers’ roles.

kaigo-completeness-drill-followup.heading: Follow responsibilities and rechecks after drills
paragraphs: Disaster preparation includes usable routes, contacts, who assists whom and accessible information, beyond supplies. A complete bag does not establish that assigned helpers can reach people needing help.
Drills test whether plans work and reveal gaps. Record unavailable contacts or routes separately from attendance numbers. Everyone attending does not establish safe completion.

For gaps, use the facility plan to confirm unfinished tasks, reporting recipients and who accepted the response. A roster differs from actual acceptance. Do not write unconfirmed substitutes or routes as decided.

Confirm correction responsibility and when and how effectiveness will be checked. Distinguish tidying or renewed contact from verified usable routes, delivered information and connected support. Use findings for future drills and plan review.

This teaches checking and reporting, not one evacuation sequence for earthquakes, fires and storms alike. In actual emergencies follow trained facility responses and instructions rather than waiting to complete a learning report.

[Learning example] Drill supplies are complete, but the helper for someone needing hearing support cannot be reached and a trolley blocks the route. Separately report checked supplies and unfinished contact/access, then confirm response and rechecking roles through the plan.

kaigo-completeness-emotion-confirm.heading: Do not determine feelings or motivation from expression alone
paragraphs: Expression and behavior are clues for questions. Silence alone does not establish sadness, anger or refusal. Ask without leading to check feelings and current wishes.
Desire to participate differs from difficult conditions. Noise, hunger, fatigue and anxiety may overlap. Preserve words and observations rather than explaining every response with one assumed cause.

Meaningful small choices can support motivation: participation form, music or topics, when and with whom to spend time. Discuss real options and conditions. More activities or staff praise do not prove satisfaction.
Consider support based on confirmed wishes and distinguish abilities from unchecked conditions. Wanting time alone now must not become refusal of all future interaction.

Needs models and expressions cannot diagnose psychology or establish decision-making ability. Respect feelings and discuss support within the individual plan. Convey specific information to responsible staff if difficulties or changes persist or otherwise require attention.

[Learning example] During music time the person speaks little and looks at the door. Asked, they say, “It is noisy, so I want to listen alone. I want to choose the music.” Separate observation and words, avoiding labels of antisocial or unmotivated, and discuss listening conditions.

kaigo-completeness-memory-transfer.heading: Distinguish familiar skills from memory for new information
paragraphs: Memory includes encoding new information, retaining it and recalling it when needed. One successful or unsuccessful task cannot assess every process.

Distinguish semantic memory for knowledge such as meanings, episodic memory for experiences such as meetings, and procedural memory for learned skills. A familiar task performed well does not establish learning a newly heard schedule.

If new information cannot be answered, first check whether it was communicated accessibly and whether content and question were understood. Do not assume memory alone is responsible without considering hearing in noisy surroundings or other conditions.

Record observed skill, replies, explanation conditions and unknowns separately. Discuss short explanations, quiet settings or accessible methods and check understanding and memory within that task’s scope.

This teaches concepts and information gathering. One forgotten schedule does not diagnose illness, and one familiar skill does not guarantee all memory is normal. This material does not replace dementia testing or assessment of decision-making ability.

[Learning example] The person folds towels skillfully but cannot answer an activity time just announced in a noisy room. Skill alone does not establish all memory as normal; check hearing and understanding too. One answer does not establish disease.

169.title: Connect specific information and questions with professionals
objectives: Create handoffs including wishes, observations and consultation questions.
Do not treat a job title as completed action or plan change.
169.context: [Learning example] Kai-san wants club participation but struggles with arranging items by hand and speaking before a group. Staff sent only “PT, please handle everything.” Separate participation wishes, observed difficulties and desired advice, then clarify responsibility and consultation contacts. The speech difficulty’s cause is not diagnosed.
169.artCaption: Discuss daily-life information such as meals with several team members around the person. The image alone does not identify professions or advice.

170.title: Record personal words, observations and measurements separately
objectives: Distinguish words, actions and measurements by source.
Correct assumed causes and arrange hazard reporting and checking.
170.context: [Learning example] At 14:00 Lien-san said, “I am tired today,” and stopped towel folding twice. Nothing was measured, but the record says “fever due to room heat.” Preserve time, words and actions, correct unconfirmed fever and cause, and report the change to the person responsible.
170.artCaption: Staff review records, separating words, observations and measurements.

171.title: Check hand-hygiene methods and completion
objectives: Distinguish methods according to visible dirt and tasks.
Check coverage, drying, recontamination and glove limits.
171.context: [Learning example] Hands are visibly dirty after collecting soiled towels. Colleagues propose hurried hand rubbing or gloves alone. Choose water and soap based on visible dirt, checking coverage, rinsing, drying and possible recontamination before the next task.
171.artCaption: Left shows drying after washing; right shows hand rubbing. Distinguish methods; the image alone does not establish every stage.

172.title: Check personal condition and working requirements first
objectives: Report back pain and missing training as support conditions.
Distinguish equipment presence from readiness for safe use.
172.context: [Learning example] A worker has back pain today and no training on the stored sliding-sheet model. Asked to reposition someone, they must not assume posture and equipment presence establish readiness. Report and check health, training, the person’s plan and helpers’ roles.
172.artCaption: Check plans and conditions around an empty bed. This is not a solo-lifting technique illustration.

173.title: Follow responsibilities and rechecks after drills
objectives: Separate supplies, contact, route and helper gaps.
Track acceptance of tasks separately from verified improvement.
173.context: [Learning example] Drill supplies are complete, but the helper for someone needing hearing support cannot be reached and a trolley blocks the route. Separately report checked supplies and unfinished contact/access, then confirm response and rechecking roles through the plan.
173.artCaption: Consider worker health and disaster supplies. Bag inspection alone does not complete contact or route checks.

174.title: Do not determine feelings or motivation from expression alone
objectives: Do not assume feelings from expressions or silence.
Ask participation wishes separately from environmental difficulties.
174.context: [Learning example] During music time the person speaks little and looks at the door. Asked, they say, “It is noisy, so I want to listen alone. I want to choose the music.” Separate observation and words, avoiding labels of antisocial or unmotivated, and discuss listening conditions.
174.artCaption: Listen to concerns; expression alone does not establish feelings or participation intent.

175.title: Distinguish familiar skills from memory for new information
objectives: Distinguish skill, knowledge and experience memories.
Check hearing and understanding without judging everything from one result.
175.context: [Learning example] The person folds towels skillfully but cannot answer an activity time just announced in a noisy room. Skill alone does not establish all memory as normal; check hearing and understanding too. One answer does not establish disease.
175.artCaption: Familiar button handling and photographs provide conversation topics. One skill or image cannot diagnose the whole of memory.

weekly-kaigo-depth-team-handoff-probe.prompt: How should “PT, handle everything” be corrected?
options: Convey participation wishes, specific manual and group-speaking difficulties, observations and questions, then clarify roles and consultation contacts.
Keep only the PT recipient and omit wishes or daily context.
Convey only arranging difficulty and ignore group speech.
Treat the sent report as a changed plan and start new exercises.
rationales: This communicates goals and specifics without inventing causes or assigning all problems to one profession.
A title alone omits support needs and personal goals.
This discards relevant difficulties without grounds.
Sending is not confirmed plan change or authority to design training.
weekly-kaigo-depth-team-handoff-probe.reading: [Practice] Kai-san wants club participation but struggles with arranging objects and speaking to a group. Staff sent only “PT, handle everything.” Causes and a new plan remain unconfirmed.

weekly-kaigo-depth-observation-evidence-.prompt: Which correction and handoff match Lien-san’s facts?
options: Staff felt hot, so preserve confirmed fever.
Without temperature, erase tiredness and two observed pauses.
Two pauses prove heat caused the problem.
Preserve 14:00 words, two pauses and unmeasured status; correct unsupported fever/cause through facility methods and report change.
rationales: Staff sensation differs from measured personal temperature.
Words and observations remain valuable despite absent measurements.
Actions alone do not establish a cause; other conditions are unknown.
This separates sources and corrects through procedure rather than deleting history.
weekly-kaigo-depth-observation-evidence-.reading: [Practice] At 14:00 Lien-san said, “I am tired today,” and stopped folding towels twice. Temperature and other measurements were not taken. The record says “fever due to room heat.”

weekly-kaigo-completeness-hand-choice-pr.prompt: With visibly dirty hands, which check is appropriate before the next task?
options: Choose the nearest hand rub without considering dirt or task.
Wash with water and soap; check both hands, rinsing and drying, no glove substitution and recontamination.
Count rubbing repetitions without checking surfaces.
Initial cleaning means no later contact needs attention.
rationales: Convenience alone is insufficient; check visible dirt and tasks.
Visible dirt needs washing with coverage and completion; gloves do not replace hygiene.
Counts do not prove thumbs or fingertips were reached.
New dirty contact can recontaminate; check contacts and timing.
weekly-kaigo-completeness-hand-choice-pr.reading: [Practice] Hands are visibly dirty after collecting soiled towels. Next is handling clean-supply containers. Colleagues suggest hurried hand rubbing or gloves alone.

weekly-kaigo-completeness-worker-capacit.prompt: With back pain and no model-specific training, what should be reported and checked first?
options: Report pain and missing training; check the person’s plan, suitable equipment, operators, teamwork and readiness.
A wide stance is enough; hide pain and missing training.
Equipment presence completes training and inspection checks.
Only the person’s ability matters, not worker condition or helpers.
rationales: This combines worker capacity with personal and task conditions rather than posture or presence alone.
Hidden health/training information prevents appropriate support arrangements.
Presence differs from model knowledge and readiness.
Worker, environment, equipment and cooperation also affect safety.
weekly-kaigo-completeness-worker-capacit.reading: [Practice] A worker has back pain and is asked to reposition someone. A sliding sheet is stored, but the worker lacks training on that model. A colleague says correct posture is enough.

weekly-kaigo-completeness-drill-followup.prompt: Supplies were checked, but a helper is unreachable and a trolley blocks the route. Which recording and follow-up are appropriate?
options: Complete the drill because the bag is ready.
Roster presence proves acceptance despite no response.
Separate supply completion from contact/route gaps and confirm response roles and recheck methods through the plan.
Assigning trolley removal proves access rechecked.
rationales: Supplies do not establish delivered information or usable access.
Assigned roster roles differ from actual contact and acceptance.
This tracks correction and verified effects without inventing substitutes or routes.
Assignment, correction and effectiveness checks are distinct stages.
weekly-kaigo-completeness-drill-followup.reading: [Practice] Drill bag supplies are checked. The helper for a person needing hearing support cannot be contacted. A trolley blocks the planned route.

weekly-kaigo-completeness-emotion-confir.prompt: Which record matches the person’s music-time wishes?
options: Little speech means refusing all future interaction.
Separate little speech/door gaze from noise-related wishes to listen alone and choose music, then discuss conditions.
Listening alone means no wish to choose music.
Many planned activities prove satisfaction and participation.
rationales: This generalizes one scene to all future interaction.
This preserves confirmed feelings and choices without diagnostic or personality assumptions.
The choice wish is explicit and cannot be canceled.
Counts cannot replace satisfaction or wish checks.
weekly-kaigo-completeness-emotion-confir.reading: [Practice] During group music, the person speaks little and looks at the door. Staff initially assume dislike of socializing. Asked, the person says, “It is noisy, so I want to listen alone. I want to choose the music.”

weekly-kaigo-completeness-memory-transfe.prompt: Towel folding is skillful but the new activity time cannot be answered. Which approach is appropriate?
options: A familiar skill proves all new-information memory normal.
One missed time is illness without hearing checks.
A noisy room proves noise is the sole cause.
Separate skill from unanswered information, check delivery and understanding and use a suitable communication method.
rationales: Skill alone guarantees neither encoding nor retention or recall.
Check hearing and understanding; one reply cannot diagnose.
Noise is relevant but actual hearing remains unconfirmed.
This distinguishes processes without guaranteeing all memory or diagnosing from one lapse.
weekly-kaigo-completeness-memory-transfe.reading: [Practice] The person folds towels skillfully but cannot answer the activity time just given in a noisy room. Staff assume folding proves all memory normal.
